coordinates.note: The MC-1 building housing the Muon g-2 storage ring is mapped in OpenStreetMap; the coordinate is the building centroid, within about 40 m of the hall and checked against the g-2 TDR layout. It is shown as approximate because OpenStreetMap is a community map and not a survey. It replaces a general Fermilab-site geocoder point of 4 km precision.

name: MC-1 building, Fermilab Muon Campus
notes: No official source consulted (checked 2026-09-18: fnal.gov paths returned 403; muon.fnal.gov PDF paths returned 404/403) gives building-level coordinates for MC-1. The point recorded is the centroid of the MC-1 building as traced in OpenStreetMap (see the coordinate note).

summary.plain: The building at Fermilab, near Chicago, that holds the 14-metre superconducting ring used by the Muon g-2 experiment to measure a tiny wobble in spinning muons.
summary.technical: MC-1 building on the Fermilab site (Muon Campus), housing the Muon g-2 (E989) storage ring, cryogenics plant and counting room. No official building-specific coordinate was found; the recorded point is the centroid of the MC-1 building as traced in OpenStreetMap (about 40 m precision), shown as approximate.
